finding.claim: With the default allow_remote_refs=None, a $ref to a local file outside the input base path (an absolute path, a ../ traversal or a file:// URL) is accepted with only a deprecation warning. HTTP(S) $ref targets are also fetched by default, with only a warning. An untrusted schema can therefore make the generator read arbitrary local files that parse as JSON/YAML, and fetch public URLs. Parsed content can reach generated output or error messages. This looks like a deliberate, documented transition default, so impact is limited and it is a low-confidence candidate.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled schema document passed to the generator (file or URL) that contains a $ref such as file:///path/outside/base.yaml or ../../outside.yaml
finding.sink: load_data_from_path(path) in _load_ref_data_from_path, and _get_text_from_url for HTTP(S) refs

trace.note: _get_ref_body dispatches by URL scheme. For allow_remote_refs None it only calls warn_deprecated for http(s) and never blocks.
_get_ref_body_from_url converts file:// to a Path via url2pathname
_resolve_local_ref_path returns resolved_path when allow_remote_refs is None, and only warns at line 10989 instead of raising
File contents are read and parsed through _load_ref_data_from_path, which calls load_data_from_path

finding.guards_checked: is_relative_to(base_path) check, enforced only when allow_remote_refs is False. The http.py SSRF guard is solid: it blocks private, loopback, legacy-IPv4 and embedded-IPv6 addresses, pins DNS, revalidates every redirect and strips credentials on cross-origin redirects. Remote file reads need the target to parse as JSON/YAML. Generated docstrings are escaped (escape_docstring) and patterns are emitted via repr. input_model.py and dynamic.py execute code, but only code the user explicitly supplies or the tool generated itself.
